analysis.title: GS Vol Views - Stankard - 11 Nov 2026
key_insights: US investor net leverage is at 5-year lows per GS PB, so positioning is light. The Panic Index is at 6.5/10, and last Thursday was the largest put volume session ever.
Fed speakers and PPI data are the macro catalysts this week, before focus shifts to NVDA earnings next week. The SPX implied move through Friday is 1.10%.

NDX average-stock 1m ATM implied vol is ~44v, which understates the concentration of pain in AI infrastructure names. GS's AI Data Center Basket (GSTMTDAT) is realizing ~80v over 1m, above its Liberation Day high.

NVDA is down nearly 30% since early October, erasing over $1.75tn of market cap, and trades at ~24x P/E, a valuation not seen since 2019. With vol and skew elevated, the desk favors long delta plus short vol with a 10% downside cushion.

Post-midterms, biopharma has drawn interest on secular tailwinds, higher M&A appetite and an expected sustained broadening trade. For the second consecutive quarter almost every large-cap biopharma company beat on the topline and the majority raised guidance.
Vol of vol had its 2nd largest single-day increase on record last Thursday, then a top-10 single-day decline on Monday. Realized vol of VVIX has surged towards all-time highs.

The desk likes owning downside skew in SPX because the Street is structurally short vol on the way down and long vol on the way up, which should keep an asymmetric bid for protection on any meaningful selloff.
Small cap vol has reset near multi-year lows. IWM vol trades near its lowest spread to SPY since Covid, and positioning is thin ahead of a seasonally strong period for small caps.
The desk prefers cross-asset hybrids for expressing macro views with more precision and leverage, following a team call on the topic last week.
